rows.reason: Wrong line: 'above his company' runs across two lines ('above his' ends line 32, 'company' starts line 33), but the script says 'Line 32 says he was 'proud' and 'above his company''. Write 'Lines 32 and 33'. The land-walks precheck fails it on the same quote. The rest is true: 'till his manners gave a disgust' is on line 31, and Bingley's 'angry that the ball closed so' is on line 37.

The speech on lines 51 and 52 holds 'I must have you dance' and ends 'You had much better dance'. 'stupid manner' is on line 52 and describes the standing about. The false claim 'It opens' has been removed.

All quotes are on the lines cited: 'no very cordial feelings' (lines 70 and 71), 'with great spirit' (line 71), 'delighted in anything ridiculous' (lines 72 and 73). It now shows the lines 72 and 73 evidence for the funny side and separates the key from the 'forgiven' and 'not bothered' options.

Wrong line: 'Named things went in the first box to be returned.' runs across two lines ('to be' ends line 7, 'returned.' starts line 8), but the script cites 'Line 7'. Write 'Lines 7 and 8'. The precheck fails it. Also 'Yet line 33 puts it in 'the Friday box'' never shows that the Friday box is the box for things with no name going to charity (lines 8 and 9), so the child cannot see which rule is bent. Name that link.

'Nothing says he adds his name.' argues from silence. A passage leaves out countless things, and this option's own tag hint tells the child to 'Find the line that proves it'. 'A place he could take and does not' then states something no line says. The script shows only that he walks past now ('passed the noticeboard', line 37). It never supports the key's future 'is not going to fill' (trials in 'September' on line 38, next to his giving away his named jumper because 'It won't fit me next year', line 47). The key is the intended reading of the writer's purpose and no other option is defensible, so the fault is in the script, not the question. Rest the step on 'passed' and on that later evidence, not on what the passage leaves out.

'It won't fit me next year.' is on line 47, 'a second or two longer than the answer needed' is on line 48 and 'the way he had folded it' is on line 49. It now explains both halves: the longer look means she doubts him, and folding it back his way lets the reason stand.

Wrong line: 'to be returned' runs across two lines ('to be' on line 7, 'returned' on line 8), but the script says 'Line 7 says ... 'to be returned''. Write 'Lines 7 and 8'. The precheck fails it. The rest is true: 'the charity collection' is on lines 8 and 9, 'had left in Year Four' is on line 13, 'anyway' is on line 14, and the step from returns-versus-charity to the key is sound.

'at about half-past five' is on line 41, 'deeply asleep' at eight o'clock is on line 39 and 'the water had all boiled away' is on line 42. 5.30 to 8.00 is two and a half hours. The false 'nobody is in the kitchen' has been removed, and the script now reaches the water boiling away and the bottom burning out.

The quotes are on the lines cited: 'how much water' (line 24), 'higher up than the field' (lines 25 and 26), 'only a bank of earth' (line 18), 'did not look over for a while' (line 26). The question asks why, and the passage never states the reason. The sentence 'Water piled up above the land, held back by earth, is an uneasy sight' is the one inference step the question requires, and it is built only from lines 18, 25 and 26 ('only a bank of earth', 'higher up than the field', 'shifting itself about'). It is given as reasoning, not presented as a claim the passage makes, so it is fair. It avoids giving the narrator a gender.
